meta.tagline: The membership register of Ghana's seventeenth region.

legal.notAGovernmentDocument: Region 17 membership is a standing in a community. It is not a government document and confers no citizenship, residence, visa, or right of entry.
legal.referral: Questions about citizenship, Right of Abode, or the Ghana Card go to Ghana's Diaspora Affairs Office or the Ministry of the Interior. We refer. We do not advise on eligibility.

card.pendingNumber: Reserved once you confirm your email

join.sub: Membership is free, permanent, and open to the global African diaspora, to Ghanaians at home, and to allies. Takes about a minute.
join.resumed: We kept what you had already entered.

step1.heading: Who you are
step1.lede: Enough to know you and to send you your credential. Nothing more.
step1.dobHint: Month and year only, never the day. Region 17 membership is for adults, 18 and over.
step1.dobMissing: Please enter your month and year of birth.
step1.underage: Region 17 membership opens at 18. We're working on a youth pathway with the safeguards it needs, and we'd rather build that properly than let you in early. Come back and find us.
step1.emailHint: Where your member number and credential go. We verify it, then leave you alone unless you ask us not to.
step1.emailMissing: Enter an email address so we can send your credential.
step1.codeLede: One short step. Confirming this address is what lets us hold a member number for you.
step1.codeLabel: Enter the code from your email
step1.codeSent: We sent a code to {email}. It expires shortly.
step1.codeResent: We sent another code to {email}. Use the most recent one.
step1.codeHint: The code confirms this address. Nothing is stored against it until you enter the code.
step1.codeMissing: Enter the code from your email.
step1.codeLength: That is not a full code. Codes are {min} to {max} digits. Enter it exactly as it appears in the email.
step1.codeWrong: That code did not match. Check the most recent email and try again.
step1.locationHint: City-level. You choose later how precisely this shows to anyone else, or whether it shows at all.
step1.genderHint: Used only for counting, so we can see whether Region 17 is reaching everyone. Never shown on your profile, never searchable, never shared with anyone including government. Skip it freely.

step2.heading: How you connect
step2.lede: Choose everything that's true. No option ranks above another, and we will never ask you to document any of it.
step2.regionsHint: Where your interest lies, not where you're from. Many members have never been. Skip it freely.

connections.africanDiasporaNote: African descent, anywhere in the world

step3.heading: What you need, what you bring
step3.lede: This is the part that makes the register work. Two sentences give another member a real reason to reach out, and give you somewhere to turn. You can add them later.
step3.askLabel: What do you need right now?
step3.askPlaceholder: Looking for a manufacturer in the Ashanti Region. Need someone who's navigated GIPC registration. Trying to find a data science mentor.
step3.offerPlaceholder: I can review a business plan. I've shipped into West Africa for eleven years. I'll talk to any young person considering medicine.
step3.roleHint: Whatever describes you. Not everyone has a job title.
step3.orgPlaceholder: Organisation, school, or your own venture

step4.heading: The Compact
step4.lede: Every member affirms this. It is what makes Region 17 a community rather than a list.
step4.compactOne: I join Ghana's seventeenth region as a member.
step4.compactTwo: I come as a contributor, not only as a visitor or a donor. What I know, what I can do, and who I know are things I am willing to offer.
step4.compactThree: I recognise that knowledge moves in both directions. I have things to learn from the continent as surely as I have things to bring to it.
step4.compactFour: I will keep my record current, represent Region 17 honestly, and treat every other member, at home and abroad, as an equal.
step4.compactSmall: I understand that this membership is a standing within a community, not a legal status, and that it grants no citizenship, residence, or right of entry. Questions about citizenship, Right of Abode, or the Ghana Card are handled by Ghana's Diaspora Affairs Office and the Ministry of the Interior. Region 17 will point you to the right office.
step4.affirm: I affirm the Region 17 Compact and agree to the Code of Conduct.
step4.consentsRecord: What we may do with your record
step4.consentsRecordHint: All off unless you turn them on. Change any of these any time in settings.
step4.handleHint: You can change this once, ever. After that it's fixed, so that members and institutions who have your address can still find you. Your member number never changes.
step4.handleLive: Your address goes live when you confirm your email.
step4.handleChecking: Checking whether that address is free.
step4.handleSuggestionsLabel: Here are some that are free. Choose one, or keep typing.
step4.footnote: Next you'll confirm your address. Your record goes live then.

consents.directory: Show me in the member directory
consents.directoryNote: Other members can find you. Your contact details stay hidden.
consents.institutions: Let vetted employers and institutions find me
consents.institutionsNote: Organisations we've verified can search for your skills. They never see your contact details; they send a request and you decide.
consents.daoop: Share my record with Ghana's Diaspora Affairs Office
consents.daoopNote: The government office that runs Ghana's official diaspora register. Separate from Region 17. Nothing is shared unless you tick this.
consents.researchNote: Anonymised, counted alongside others, for the State of the Ghanaian Diaspora report. Never identifiable.
consents.townhallNote: Monthly, one region at a time. Roughly one email a month.
consents.programmesNote: When something opens that matches what you've told us.

handleErrors.empty: Choose an address so members can find you.
handleErrors.tooShort: An address needs at least three characters.
handleErrors.tooLong: An address can be at most thirty characters.
handleErrors.format: Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. Start and end with a letter or number.
handleErrors.taken: That address is taken. Try another.
handleErrors.reserved: That address is reserved. Try another.

issued.foundingNote: You joined before {date}. That standing closes on that date and will never be offered again.
issued.addressPending: Live once you activate your record.
issued.nextOne: Confirm your address. That activates your record and puts your address live.
issued.nextTwo: Add your Ask and your Offer. It's the reason members find each other.
issued.nextThree: The next Regional Spotlight town hall is on the 14th. Your seat is free.
issued.incomplete: Your record is entered, but we could not save everything: {items}. Try again so your register entry is complete.
issued.retry: Save the rest of my record

recovery.expired: Your place was held while you filled this in, and that hold has now expired. Here is your number. Everything you entered is still here.
recovery.claimed: The number we were holding went to another registration while you were away. Here is your number. Everything you entered is still here.
recovery.unknown: We could not find the number we were holding for you. Here is your number. Everything you entered is still here.

challenge.unavailable: The check that protects member numbers is not available right now, so we can't issue one yet. Nothing you did caused this. Try again in a moment. If it keeps happening, write to us and we will sort it out.
challenge.failed: The check that protects member numbers did not pass, so we can't give you one yet. No number was taken and nothing was lost.
challenge.expired: The check that protects member numbers did not finish in time, so we can't give you one yet. No number was taken.
challenge.kept: Everything you entered is still here. You'll be able to continue as soon as this check passes.
challenge.stillStuck: Still not going through after a few tries?
challenge.contactSupport: Email {email} and we'll get you your number by hand.
challenge.stub: Development build: the member-number check is stubbed and no real challenge is running. This does not exist in a production build.

authLink.expiredBody: Confirmation links are short-lived on purpose, and this one has passed its window. It will not open your record.
authLink.deniedHeading: That link could not be used.
authLink.deniedBody: It has either been used already or it was opened in a different browser from the one that asked for it.
authLink.unknownBody: We could not tell what went wrong with it. Usually that means it has already been used, or it has expired.
authLink.held: If a member number was being held for you, it is still yours. If the hold has lapsed we issue a new one and keep everything you entered.
authLink.joinAgain: Ask for a fresh code below. Everything you entered is still here.

verify.lede: Your address was confirmed by the code you entered when you joined. This puts your record and your Region 17 address live.
verify.successLede: Your record is active and your address is live.
verify.noMember: This account has not joined yet.
verify.emailUnconfirmed: We could not confirm this address. Sign in again and we will send a fresh code.
verify.emailMismatch: The address you confirmed is not the address on this record. Sign in with the address you joined with.
verify.notPending: This record is not awaiting verification. Go to your membership to see where it stands.

declare.heading: What brings you
declare.lede: One line. It is how the platform knows what to bring you, and you can change it or add another whenever you like.

headline.label: Say it in your own words
headline.hint: Short and specific beats broad. This is what a region sees.

note.label: Anything worth knowing
note.hint: Optional. Background, scale, how you usually work.

consent.heading: What we may do with it
consent.matchingRequired: We will use this to tell you when a region posts something that fits. That is what a declaration is for, so it is not optional. Everything below is, and you can change any of it in settings.
consent.directory_visibility: Show me in the member directory, so other members can find me by what I offer.
consent.programme_updates: Send me programme updates for the places I follow.
consent.institutional_discoverability: Let verified regional bodies see this declaration.

declare.failed: That did not save. Try again, and if it keeps failing tell us.
declare.window: Your declaration runs for eighteen months. Renewing it is one tap, and it lapses quietly rather than going stale.

meta.title: The seventeenth region | Region 17
meta.description: Ghana counts sixteen regions at home. The seventeenth is the global African diaspora, and Charter Membership is how the family gets counted.
meta.ogTitle: There is a version of Ghana that lives outside Ghana. We are it.
meta.ogDescription: The declaration did not create us. It caught up with us. Add your name to the Charter.

atlas.alt: A map of the seventeenth region: a black star at Ghana, joined by threads to sixteen cities where the diaspora already lives. Toronto, New York, Washington, Havana, Kingston, Port of Spain, Cartagena, Salvador, Sao Paulo, London, Amsterdam, Berlin, Paris, Dubai, Johannesburg and Sydney. Light travels out from Ghana to each city and back again.

stanza1.line1: There is a version of Ghana that lives outside Ghana.

stanza2.body: We kept the language. We sent something home on the first of the month without being asked. We built the clinics and the school blocks and the boreholes, through associations meeting in church halls, in cities Ghana has never had on any map.

stanza3.lead: In December 2025 the President said out loud what we have always been.
stanza3.sub: The declaration did not create us. It caught up with us.

still.line1: A region is not a line on a map.
still.line2: It is a place where people can be found
still.line3: by name, and reached when opportunity comes looking.
still.closeLead: So when there is work in Kumasi that needs exactly what you do,

ledger.ledeHome: Ghana counts sixteen regions at home.
ledger.aside: No borders. Everywhere we already are, written down.

branches.bornInBody: You left with a suitcase and a promise. The promise still stands.
branches.bornToBody: Raised abroad on jollof Sundays and long phone calls home. You never needed a stamp to belong.
branches.descendedBody: Through the Americas, the Caribbean, Europe. The ocean took much. It did not take the thread.
branches.continentBody: Nigerian, Senegalese, Kenyan, all of us. Ghana's door has never been closed to the continent.
branches.returnedBody: Already home, or packing. Your seat is warm on both sides of the ocean.
branches.friendsBody: Married in, moved in, or simply moved by it. Chosen family counts as family here.
branches.close: Six ways of carrying Ghana. One standing, no tiers. Every one of them begins with a name.

window.only: It opens 5 October. It closes 31 January.
window.onlyAfter: Every year after this one has a Cohort.
window.hinge: Home cannot know your name until it is written.
window.fineprint: Free for family. Always. Three minutes to be counted.
window.credit: Lifetime patron plaque presented at the Region 17 launch, Washington D.C.

index.body: Take a deep dive into each of our sixteen regions and see where you fit. Every region has its own page, its own plans, and its own ways in.

regions.ahafo: Ghana's green newcomer: cocoa farms around Goaso, sacred groves, forest reserves. One of the youngest regions in the country, which means the ground floor is still wide open for family who want in early.
regions.ashanti: Kumasi, the Golden Stool, and the living heart of Asante heritage. The region most of our families trace first, and a manufacturing and trade engine second only to Accra.
regions.bono: Sunyani, regularly named Ghana's cleanest city, surrounded by cashew and cocoa country. A quiet powerhouse that has sent teachers, nurses, and farmers across the world for generations.
regions.bono-east: Techiman hosts one of West Africa's largest food markets, moving yam, maize, and cashew by the truckload. Kintampo's falls mark the old geographic centre of Ghana.
regions.central: Cape Coast and Elmina: the castles, the Door of No Return, and the ground where the diaspora's homecoming began. Also Ghana's densest concentration of historic schools.
regions.eastern: Akosombo's dam lit the nation. Aburi's gardens, Koforidua's beads, and the Akwapim hills sit an hour from Accra, which is why so many families keep land here.
regions.greater-accra: The capital region: Accra's energy, Tema's port, and W.E.B. Du Bois's resting place. The front door most of us walk through first, and the seat of the AfCFTA.
regions.north-east: Nalerigu, seat of Mamprugu, one of the oldest kingdoms in Ghana. Shea and groundnut country where traditional governance still runs deep and steady.
regions.northern: Tamale is one of West Africa's fastest-growing cities, and Larabanga's mud-and-stick mosque has stood since the 1400s. The north's commercial anchor.
regions.oti: Along Lake Volta's eastern shore: fishing towns, yam country, and the Breast Mountains. Carved out in 2019 and still writing its first chapter, with room in it for us.
regions.savannah: Ghana's largest region by land. Mole National Park's elephants, the old Gonja kingdom, Larabanga at its edge. Big sky, deep history, wide-open opportunity.
regions.upper-east: Bolgatanga's baskets travel the world; Paga's crocodiles greet visitors by name. Smart irrigation is turning dry-season farming into year-round business.
regions.upper-west: Wa's historic mosque, the hippo sanctuary at Wechiau, and some of the warmest hosting culture in Ghana. Shea country with serious agribusiness headroom.
regions.volta: Lake Volta, Wli Falls, Mount Afadja, and the Aflao border where Ghana meets West African trade. The corridor Ghana has named its next economy. Early still means something here.
regions.western: Takoradi's oil, gas, and harbour; Nzulezu standing on stilts; beaches running to the border. Where Ghana's energy economy meets the sea.
regions.western-north: Deep-forest cocoa heartland around Sefwi Wiawso, source of much of the chocolate the world eats, and home to one of Africa's most unexpected communities of faith.
